mt_lost_wall.blurb: A secluded spot in the forested hills northwest of Kalispell, in the Flathead Valley. The main draw is bouldering: nine problems on a talus field below the wall, mostly around V5 with a couple of easier ones and a single harder line. Above them are a small number of routes, a 5.9 trad crack, a long bolted line in the 5.10 range and a 5.11 sport route. Expect a quiet, adventurous feel instead of crowds, with a flat campsite near the base. Rain can leave the wall damp, though the sun tends to dry it out by midday.

mt_parking_lot_wall.blurb: The small cliff beside the trailhead in Blodgett Canyon, in the Bitterroot Mountains west of Hamilton. Unlike the long multi-pitch spires that dominate the canyon, this wall is bolt-heavy single-pitch climbing, about 800 feet wide with only a modest number of lines. A dozen routes are here, a mix of sport and trad, most of them 5.10 to 5.11 with one easier and one 5.12. Because the wall sits so close to the road end, the walk is trivial, making it a handy quick stop before or after a bigger objective in the canyon. Bitterroot rock can be scaly, so check holds.

mt_tor_rock.blurb: A single-pitch crag in the Lolo Pass area southwest of Missoula, on a forest road off Highway 12. Routes run about 80 feet at most, and the climbing is steep, mostly on faces with a few cracks, on generally good rock. There are twelve lines, seven sport and five trad, ranging from 5.9 to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11, so beginners will find little here. Some leads have only a few bolts and finish at a ramp with a walk-off. Because the walk from the car is only a couple of minutes, it is one of the busier crags in the area.

mt_wafers_the.blurb: The main climbing area at Revenue Flats, on public land between Norris and McAllister in southwest Montana. Rock fins on every side give the place an enclosed feel and can break the wind, and it is fun to scramble around. Roughly a dozen routes, mostly short single-pitch sport lines with some trad and a top-rope, run from very easy through 5.10 up to a single 5.12, plus a lone easy boulder problem. Routes often share a common belay area and ropes. Heavy use and little shade make it a popular spring destination rather than a summer one.
